{"Key findings: The definition of the informal economy is not yet widely agreed upon, with varying definitions across countries and institutions. The International Labour Organization (ILO) defines undeclared work as economic activities that are not covered or insufficiently covered by formal arrangements. The ILO's Recommendation No. 204 aims to facilitate the transition from the informal to formal economy. Research suggests that tax burden, labour market rigidity, and institutional efficiency have a significant impact on the scale of the informal economy. Higher marginal rates of income tax and higher levels of salaries in the formal sector can reduce undeclared employment. ['The Human Development Report for 2015 focuses on work and its relationship with human development.', 'Montenegro has made significant progress in human development since gaining independence, with improvements in life expectancy, education, and income.', 'In 2014, Montenegro was ranked among the 49 most prosperous countries with a very high level of human development.', "The country's HDI value decreased by 9.2% due to inequalities in income, but this is smaller than the average loss for Europe and Central Asia (13.0%) and countries with very high HDIs (12.1%).", "Montenegro's ranking according to its GNI level is 27 places lower than its rank based on all components of human development.", 'The informal economy is a significant issue in Montenegro, with the dominant proportion of self-employed individuals.', 'Formalization policies should aim to ensure the least painful transfer from undeclared to declared employment and promote decent work.', 'The report emphasizes the need for an institutional environment that motivates formalization of work in the informal sector.']

["Montenegro's HDI value of 0.802 is significantly lower than countries with very high HDIs (22.5% reduction), and 16.6% lower than ECA countries.", 'In 2014, Montenegro had a life expectancy at birth 5.4 years higher than Norway, but the income per capita was only four times as high.', 'Montenegro is above-average in Europe and Central Asia, ranking 49th globally.', 'The country has a relatively low gender inequality index (GII) of 0.172, placing it 37th out of 155 countries.', 'In 2014, the GDI value for Montenegro was 0.954, indicating a gap between genders in human development.', 'Multidimensional poverty affects approximately 3,000 individuals (0.5% of the population) in Montenegro.', 'The median age in Montenegro is 37.4 years, lower than the EU average of 42.2 years.', "Montenegro's population is projected to decrease starting around 2030, with a high level of undeclared work increasing vulnerability among the elderly."]
